title: On an exclusion, suspension or revocation list, and still in the payment file
question: Did Medicaid pay for services billed by, or attributed to, a provider number after it was put on a federal or State list?
finding: Of 16 listed provider numbers that appear anywhere in the San Francisco and Bay Area payment extract, 1 shows payments in a calendar year after the year of listing, $47,207 in all; the largest is St. Francis Medical Group, P.C. ($47,207).
how: Provider numbers on the federal exclusion list, the federal list of revoked Medicare enrollments, California's Medi-Cal suspended list and the national registry's deactivated numbers were matched to the payment file by number only (never by name). A row means money in a calendar year after the listing year. The payment file ends in December 2024, so anything listed in 2024 or later cannot show here.
limits: Exact number matches only, so anyone listed without a provider number is missed. A Medicare revocation does not by itself end Medicaid enrollment at once; the State has to act. A deactivated number often means retirement, death or a merger, and late claims for earlier care can be paid afterward. The file shows the month of service, not the day, so only whole later years are counted. Being named as the place of service is not the same as being paid.
